Petroleum and Petrochemical
Investment Regions
*121. SHRI JANARDHANA
POOJARY: Will the Minister of
PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are
establishing Petroleum and Petrochemical
Investment Regions (PPCIR) in identified
ports, including Mangalore Port;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether certain major international
oil companies have evinced interest in the
proposed project;
(d) if so, the details thereof;
(e) whether the prospective investors
have aired some concerns over infrastructure
constraints, multiple clearances, tardy
litigation process and labour laws;
(f) if so, the details thereof and in what
manner Government propose to address
their concerns;

Investment Regions are also proposed to
be established; and
(h) if so, the details thereof and the
locations identified for the purpose?
Permission for opening bank
branches in foreign countries
*122. SHRI AMAR SINGH:
SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a few Public
Sector Banks have sought permission for
opening up of their branches in foreign
countries;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the details of the decision so far taken
thereon and by when the remaining requests
are likely to be acceded to?

†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
RBI Governor's meeting with Indian
Banks' Association
*123. SHRI PRASANTA
CHATTERJEE: Will the Minister of
FINANCE be pleased to refer to answer to
Unstarred Question 4014 given in the Rajya
Sabha on 23rd May, 2006 and state:
(a) whether any pre-credit policy meeting
was held between Governor, Reserve Bank
of India and Indian Banks' Association on
28th March, 2006; and
(b) what are the details of the
submissions made by the Chief Executive
of Indian Banks' Association in this meeting?
Budgetary support to PSUs for
payment of salaries
*124. SHRI C. RAMACHANDRAIAH:
Will the Minister of HEAVY INDUSTRIES
AND PUBLIC ENTERPRISES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government are giving
budgetary support to various loss making
Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) to clear
the outstanding payment of salaries and
statutory dues to their employees;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the details of the budgetary support
provided to each loss making PSU during
each of the last two years for industries
located in Andhra Pradesh?
Additional investment by ONGC
†*125. SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
Will the Minister of  PETROLEUM
AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that ONGC has
decided to make additional investment of
Rs. 4800 crore in order to increase
production of indigenous crude oil in the
year 2006-07;
(b) if so, the total annual amount of
additional investment made for increase in
production from April 2003-04 to March
2006-07;
(c) whether the increase in the
production post investment has also been
estimated; and
(d) if so, the quantity of likely additional
production during the current year?
Tax on interest paid to senior citizens
by banks
*126. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the interest
paid to senior citizens by banks and post
offices on investments made by them on
Senior Citizen Savings Scheme has been
made taxable income;
(b) if so, the reasons for bringing senior
citizens under tax net even under the above
Scheme which is meant exclusively for senior
citizens without any tax commitment; and
(c) what are the reasons for bringing
them under the tax net now when the
scheme was introduced in 2004 and banks
and post offices have so far not been
deducting any tax on investments so made
during the last two years by senior citizens?
Profit on petrol and diesel
*127. SHRI VIJAYKUMAR RUPANI:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) the margin of profit of private and

40
public sector oil-companies per litre of
petrol and diesel; and
(b) the total amount of tax, duties,
excise etc. on petrol and diesel per litre?
New airport in Assam for
Asian Safari
*128. SHRIMATI SYEDA ANWARA
TAIMYUR: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the a private
Thai airline operator has proposed making
the State part of an Asian Safari circuit and
is interested in building an airport in Assam;
(b) whether the Bangkok Airways is
interested in building an airport near the
Kaziranga National Park and other facilities
to make Assam an Asian Safari Destination;
and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Inadequate supply of gas to two gas
turbines at Ramgarh Gas Thermal
Power Station
*129. DR. NARAYAN SINGH
MANAKLAO : Will the Minister of
PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the quantity
of gas required to operate two gas turbines
at Ramgarh Gas Thermal Power Station
(RGTPS), District Jaisalmer is inadequate;
(b) if so, the details of demand and supply
in gas;
(c) how the shortfall is being met or
proposed to be met; and
(d) by when the requisite quantity of gas
will be supplied to run both gas turbines at
full load?
Demand of States for transfer of dams
*130. DR. M.A.M. RAMASWAMY:
Will the Minister of WATER RESOURCES
be pleased to state:
(a) whether some State Governments
have demanded transfer of dams situated
in their territorial areas;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) what is the reaction of the Central
Government in this regard?
Outsourcing of works in Income Tax
department
*131. SHRI PRAVEEN RASHTRA-
PAL: Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Ministry
had resorted to outsourcing of works in the
Income Tax department;
(b) whether the Ministry have
consulted the recognised Income Tax
Employees Federation before resorting to
outsourcing; and
(c) whether the Ministry have provided
adequate computer infrastructure to the
Income Tax department?
Leasing of aircrafts by private airlines
*132. SHRIMATI MOHSINA
KIDWAI:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have directed
the private airlines not to take aircraft on
dry lease from International Airlines or
leasing companies that are part of an airline;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and

41
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(c) what action Government propose
to take in this regard?
JBICs loan package for socio-economic
development
*133. SHRI RUDRA NARAYAN
PANY:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Japan Bank
for International Cooperation (JBIC)
proposes to extend Rs. 6,000 crore loan
package towards social and economic
development in India;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) what are the details of projects that
are proposed to be financed out of this loan
inter-alia those falling in the State of Orissa?
Leaning minarets of Taj
*134. SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA
SEKAR REDDY: Will the Minister of
CULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the leading experts have
studied the leaning minarets of  Taj;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the recommendations so far received
from the experts; and
(d) the action taken thereon?
New security equipments at
airports
*135. SHRI VEDPRAKASH P.
GOYAL: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have decided to prepare a security blueprint
for all major airports and also install Bio
Matrix Equipments and CCTV facility;
(b) if so, what is the time frame for
these security arrangements to become
functional at all major airports; and
(c) what is the modus operandi of this
hi-tech security facility along with the
details thereof?
Maintenance of Kamakhaya Temple
in Assam
†*136. SHRI DWIJENDRA NATH
SHARMAH: Will the Minister of
CULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) the amount provided by Government
during the last three years for preservation
and maintenance of Kamakhaya Temple,
situated in Assam State;
(b) whether Government have
formulated any plan for beautification of the
said temple; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Tourism industry
*137. SHRIMATI S.G. INDIRA: Will
the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the tourism
industry has progressed during the last few
years;
(b) whether it is also a fact that the country
could not progress to that desired level due to
lack of infrastructure that is required for the
growth of tourism industry; and
(c) whether it is also a fact that tourists
from abroad are afraid to come to India due
to prevailing law and order problems?

Absorption of GTB employees in
Oriental Bank of Commerce
*138. SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI: Will
the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to
state:
(a) what is the number of employees of
the Global Trust Bank who have been
absorbed in the Oriental Bank of Commerce;
(b) whether these employees have been
debarred from the pensionary benefits
whereas the employees of Oriental Bank of
Commerce who were recruited even after
the merger of G.T.B. in O.B.C. are entitled
to this facility; and
(c) if so, what are the specific reasons
for the discriminatory treatment to them and
by when it would be removed?
Irrigated agricultural land
*139. DR. GYAN PRAKASH
PILANIA:
SHRI RUDRA NARAYAN
PANY:
Will the Minister of WATER
RESOURCES be pleased to state:
(a) the total non-cultivable land in the
country, the average percentage of irrigated
agricultural land all over the country, the
total agricultural land and out of this total
land under irrigation;
(b) the details of programme,with target
to enhance this percentage;
(c) whether Government have decided
to make nearly 90,000 hectares additional
agricultural land irrigable by March, 2009;
(d) if so, the details thereof and how
much expenditure would be incurred;
(e) whether any time-bound annual
target has been fixed;
(f) whether any survey has been
undertaken to find new sources of water
for increasing irrigation potential; and
(g) if so, the details thereof?
Renovation of Jamadarpali
airstrip
*140. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Jamadarpali airstrip near
Sambalpur is in shambles;
(b) whether this airport has become a
necessity considering fast growth of
Rengali-Jharsugudu corridor and fast
industrialization of its surroundings;
(c) whether Government propose to
repair and renovate the airport to boost
economy of this backward region; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor?

RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for WRITTEN ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday,  the August 1, 2006/Sravana 10, 1928 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Civil Aviation; Company Affairs; Culture; Finance; Heavy
Industries and Public Enterprises; Petroleum and Natural Gas;
Tourism; Water Resources)
Total number of questions — 154
164
Growth opportunities in aviation
sector
710. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have
introduced number of measures and steps
i.e. modernisation of airports, new aircrafts
ordered, ATF excise duty halved, travel
tax abolished and landing charges reduced
etc.;
(b) if so, whether some more initiatives
are yet to be taken for growth
opportunities in aviation sector;
(c) whether Government have
demonstrated its commitment by
launching the airport modernisation
programme to ensure speedy
implementation (both at major hubs and
35 small airports) to match with the traffic
growth; and
(d) if so, what are the main steps
considered and to what extent it has been
successful?
Expansion of civil aviation industry
711. SHRI KARNENDU
BHATTACHARJEE: Will the Minister of
CIVIL AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether India at the Annual General
Meeting of the International Air Transport
Association (IATA) held at Paris this year,
indicated an elaborate plan for expansion
of Civil Aviation industry both in the public
and private sector;
(b) if so, the details thereof indicating
plans for expansion of industry in the
domestic and international sector to
unshackle it from the restrictive policies of
the past; and
(c) the steps taken and being taken in
pursuance thereof?
Security clearance for airlines
712. SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) the details pertaining to the
requirement for private commercial airlines
to obtain ‘security clearance’ from
Government;

165
(b) the details of security clearances
issued to airlines operating commercial
flights in India showing the date of
commencement of commercial flight
operation by each;
(c) whether security clearance pertaining
to the Promoters and Directors of M/s Jet
Air had been pending to be issued;
(d) if so, details thereof, indicating the
reasons for its remaining pending;
(e) the basis of permitting the said
Airlines to operate despite non-issuance
of security clearance;
(f) whether the same have since been
issued; and
(g) if so, details thereof?
New airline service in Kerala
713. SHRI K.E. ISMAIL: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) whether the State Government of
Kerala supported project of starting a new
airline by Cochin International Airport Ltd.
(CIAL) has been presented to the Central
Government;
(b) if so, what are the reasons for which
the Central Government are delaying
sanction to this project; and
(c) what steps would be taken to
expedite the same?
Infrastructure bottlenecks faced by
airports
714. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are working
on developing not only the airports in
the metro cities but also in at least 35
non-metro cities using public-private
partnership at Rs. 7000-8000 crore;
(b) whether Government are considering
checking the infrastructure bottlenecks
being faced at airports around the country;
(c) whether Planning Commission is
considering relaxation of environmental
clearance norms for these airports including
complete exemption from environmental
clearance for development, construction
and expansion;
(d) if so, to what extent this will help in
completing the projects; and
(e) whether Airports Authority of India
has started developing these airports?
Technical check-up of aircrafts
715. SHRI THENNALA G.
BALAKRISHNA PILLAI: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) the total number of flights operating
in the country which are owned by various
companies, company-wise;
(b) whether the DGCA has any
permanent arrangement for the regular
technical check-ups for over all conditions
of the flights; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Complaints against private airlines
716. SHRI C. PERUMAL: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government have received
any complaints regarding functioning of
private airlines, especially customer service;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the action taken against those airlines
providing inadequate services?

166
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Increase in flying age of pilots
717. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have recently
increased flying age of pilots from 60 to 65
years subject to certain conditions;
(b) if so, the details of conditions subject
to which Government would enhance flying
age of pilots;
(c) the efforts Government are making
to upgrade IGRUA to increase output of
trainees from present 40 trainees per year;
(d) to what extent flying training
institutes in Andhra Pradesh like Andhra
Pradesh Aviation Academy, Flytech
Academy and Wings Aviation help in
increasing flying trainees in the country;
and
(e) the reasons for not setting up of
more flying institutions in the country to
meet its requirements?
Re-employment of retired pilots
†718. MS. SUSHILA TIRIYA:
SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) since when the shortage of pilots in
Indian and other airlines is being felt;
(b) the estimated shortage of the pilots
in the country at present;
(c) whether the services of retired pilots
in different airlines are being taken;
(d) what are the arrangements about
their health check up prior to their moving
for the flight; and
(e) what steps have been taken by
Government to remove the shortage of the
pilots?
Shortage of skilled pilots
719. SHRI SAMAN PATHAK:
SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA:
SHRI C. PERUMAL:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether any steps are being taken
by Government to address the shortfall of
skilled pilots for the fast growing aviation
industry;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Aircrafts with Alliance Air
†720. SHRI KRISHAN LAL
BALMIKI: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) the number of aircrafts of Indian and
Alliance Air;
(b) the number of aircrafts which are
not in operation;
(c) the number of aircrafts taken on lease
and the details of the number of aircrafts
operating out of them; and
(d) the time by when the aircrafts
standing in hangars for technical reasons
will be capable of flying and the details of
loss incurred by Indian now for this
reason?
Modernisation of Dabolim airport
721. SHRI SHANTARAM LAXMAN
NAIK: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Dabolim airport in Goa
is proposed to be modernised;
(b) if so, the total amount of expenditure
likely to be incurred on each of the items

167
proposed to be undertaken for
modernisation;
(c) whether the Indian Navy has assured
additional land to the Airports Authority
of India for the purpose; and
(d) if so, the details of the land, including
its area?
Funds from privatisation of airports
722. SHRIMATI S.G. INDIRA: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
are considering to divert the funds generated
from the privatisation of Kolkata and
Chennai airports, for the purpose of
modernisation of other airports in the
country;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) what are the airports being
considered by Government for
modernisation?
Distance between domestic and
international airports
723. SHRIMATI HEMA MALINI:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
there is considerable distance between
domestic and international airports in the
country which causes lots of
inconveniences besides time to travellers;
(b) if so, whether Government are
considering to take effective steps to
address the inconveniences to air travellers;
(c) if so, by when it is expected to be
implemented; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Delay in flights of Indian airlines
724. SHRI K.E. ISMAIL: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) what are the reasons for the delay of
almost all flights of Indian Airlines could
the Minister make a statement how many
flights of Indian Airlines flew in time from
all destinations during the last three
months;
(b) whether Government are aware that
there is no direct flight to Trivandrum from
Delhi for more than two months; if so, the
reasons for it and how long it would
continue like this; and
(c) whether as promised a flight to Delhi
in the morning from Trivandrum would be
operated soon in addition to what was there
previously?
Development of Trivandrum airport
725. SHRI THENNALA G.
BALAKRISHNA PILLAI: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government have any
proposal for the development of
Trivandrum International Airport;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the total amount earmarked for this
purpose?
Improvement in infrastructure of pilot
training schools
726. SHRI EKANATH K. THAKUR:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
the lack of infrastructure and instructors in
Indian pilot training schools is taking a toll
on pilot training education in the country;

168
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(b) whether it is a fact that 50 pilot
training schools in the country have closed
the shop in the last six months and India is
left with just 30 pilot training schools now;
and
(c) if so, the steps proposed by
Government to improve the infrastructure
in Indian pilot training schools?
Non-functional X-ray machines at
airports
727. DR. M.A.M. RAMASWAMY:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) the steps taken by Government to
safeguard the airport installations in the
country;
(b) whether Government are aware that
X-ray machines installed at the airports
are not functioning efficiently; and
(c) if so, the action taken by Government
to further safeguard the vital aviation
installations?
Development of infrastructure at
airports
†728. SHRI RUDRA NARAYAN
PANY: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) the details of airlines and aeroplanes
presently operating in the country;
(b) how many passengers travel daily
by air on an average;
(c) whether Government are taking any
steps in the direction of infrastructure
development for the convenience of
passengers in the airports keeping in view
the revolution in air services; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Shortage of engineers with airlines
729. SHRI MOINUL HASSAN: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Indian Airlines have enough
qualified engineers; and
(b) if not, whether Government are
compromising with the questionable quality
of aircraft maintenance procedures and the
reasons therefor?
Working of foreigners as pilots
730. SHRI MOINUL HASSAN: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) the number of foreign nationals
working as commanders to meet the
shortage of pilots; and
(b) the policy of Government to
improve employment prospects of many
youngsters in India?
Boeing Company’s overhaul hub at
Nagpur
731. SHRI TARIQ ANWAR: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Boeing
Company is going to set a maintenance,
repair overhaul hub in Nagpur for planes;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) how much time it will take to get it
operational?
Operation of non-scheduled airlines
732. SHRI MAHENDRA MOHAN:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) the names and other details of non-

169
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
scheduled airlines operating in the country;
(b) the percentage share of these airlines
in the Indian domestic aviation market;
(c) the cities between which these
airlines are presently operating/proposed
to operate and the broad time-table and
fare structure being followed by them; and
(d) the details of guidelines laid-down
for equity norms and other regulatory
requirements for such airlines?
New airports
733. SHRIMATI VIPLOVE THAKUR:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether a plan for renovation and
expansion of airports in the country
particularly in Himachal Pradesh is under
the consideration of Government;
(b) if so, the amount, if any, spent
thereon so far and the current status of
each work; and
(c) the steps initiated so far to set up
new airports in the country, State-wise?
Development of airports in Himachal
Pradesh
734. SHRIMATI VIPLOVE
THAKUR: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether the air facilities in Himachal
Pradesh are very poor;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether there is any proposal with
Government for the development of the
existing airports and setting up of new
airports in the State;
(d) if so, the details thereof;
(e) the time by which the work is
expected to be completed; and
(f) the total expenditure involved in
these projects?
National Aeronautics Commission
†735. SHRI UDAY PRATAP SINGH:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
constitute a National Aeronautics
Commission for better co-ordination and
management between civil and military
aviation; and
(b) if so, the details thereof?
Disconnection of PM’s aircraft with
control tower
736. SHRI SHAHID SIDDIQUI:
SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
while landing, the Prime Minister's aircraft
got disconnected with the control tower of
the Delhi airport;
(b) if so, for how long the aircraft
remained disconnected with the control
tower;
(c) the reasons for such a disconnection
and the negligence on the part of the
concerned authorities who are responsible
for this; and
(d) what certainty are there that such
incidents shall not be occur in future?
MNCs in Andhra Pradesh
737. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI: Will the Minister of
COMPANY AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) how many MNCs, including foreign

170
companies, have set up their offices in
Andhra Pradesh during the past three years;
(b) whether these companies have ever
approached the Central Government for
allowing them some facilities/concessions
in connection with setting up their offices
in the State; and
(c) what facilities/concessions have
been extended to them in this regard so far
and what is the impact thereof?
Amendment to Companies Act
738. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN:
Will the Minister of  COMPANY
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have any
proposal to bring amendments to the
Companies Act;
(b) if so, the details of the proposal;
(c) whether the views of the companies
representatives have been obtained; and
(d) by when the Bill is likely to be
finalised?
Action against misleading
advertisements
†739. SHRI JAI PARKASH
AGGARWAL: Will the Minister of
COMPANY AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether according to the
Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices
Commission (MRTPC) misleading adver-
tisements being issued with the objective
of attracting customers by companies
